examples.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
y' + 3y = 26 \sin(2x), \qquad y(0) =  1
$$

Given that the differential equation 

$$
y' + 3y = 26 \sin(2x)
$$

has the complementary solution $y_c = Ae^{-3x},$ solve the initial value problem.
examples.worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution $y_c$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
y_c' + 3y_c = 0.
$$

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is

$$
y_c  = Ae^{-3x}
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now need to find the particular solution $y_p(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $26 \sin(2x).$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
y_p(x) = \alpha \cos(2x) + \beta  \sin(2x).
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of $y_p$ gives

$$
y_p' =   - 2\alpha \sin(2x) +  2\beta \cos(2x)
$$

To find the values of $\alpha,$ and $\beta,$ we substitute $y_p$ and $y_p'$ into the differential equation:

$$
( - 2\alpha \sin(2x) +  2\beta \cos(2x)) + 3 (\alpha \cos(2x)+ \beta  \sin(2x)) = 26 \sin(2x)
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(2\beta+3\alpha)\cos(2x) + (-2\alpha +3 \beta) \sin(2x) = 26 \sin(2x).
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2\beta +3\alpha =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)) \\ -2\alpha +3\beta =26\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha=-4, \beta=6.$

Therefore, the particular solution $y_p(x)$ is

$$
y_p(x) =  - 4\cos(2x) + 6\sin(2x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x) = y_c(x)+y_p(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y =  Ae^{-3x} - 4\cos(2x) + 6\sin(2x).
$$

Now, we can find the constant $A$ using the initial conditions.

Substituting $y(0) =1$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A{e}^{-3\cdot 0}-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0)+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 0) & =1 \\ A-4+0 & =1 \\ A & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y = 5e^{-3x} - 4\cos(2x) + 6\sin(2x).
$$

To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
5\frac{\text{d}{y}_{c}}{\text{d}x}-10{y}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{2x}
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x),
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-4\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+4\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
5(-4\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+4\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x))-10(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x))=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(20\beta -10\alpha )\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+(-20\alpha -10\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}20\beta -10\alpha =3\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)) \\ -20\alpha -10\beta =-7\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =\frac{11}{50},\beta =\frac{13}{50}.$

Therefore, 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\frac{11}{50}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+\frac{13}{50}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{2x}+(\frac{11}{50})\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+(\frac{13}{50})\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$
